Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: Civil ID↔Electoral register data sharing operational: suspended/terminated IDs shared with electoral commission. CNE implemented technological platform for electoral registration/identification. Electoral ID cards issued for candidates, observers. Partial integration confirmed.
revision_notes: Both cited sources fetched: the World Bank Angola Digital Economy Diagnostic (2020/2023) and the Paradigm Initiative digital ID policy brief (2024). Neither source explicitly documents the specific claim in Comments about suspended/terminated ID sharing, though the Paradigm brief does confirm CNE ran a dedicated technological platform issuing electoral ID cards to candidates, observers, journalists and police for the 2022 elections. A targeted search of Angola's electoral law (Lei 8/15, as amended by Lei 21/21 de 2021 and Lei 13/25 de 2025) found stronger, primary-source confirmation: the electoral register database (BDCM) is legally required to be populated automatically from the national ID database (BDIC), with mandated intercommunication with the Criminal Records database to flag citizens whose political rights are suspended, and annual/on-request transmission of the citizens' file (FICM) to the CNE. The AU Election Observation Mission report on the 2022 general elections corroborates that this pipeline operates but imperfectly (e.g. dead voters found on published lists, limited transparency in list disclosure). This supports the existing Value Code of 4 (Partially integrated) - integration is real and legally mandated but not complete, given continuing manual/presencial registration for those without a Bilhete de Identidade and acknowledged data-quality gaps. Score confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Angola's electoral register - the Base de Dados dos Cidadãos Maiores (BDCM) - is legally required to be populated automatically from the national civil identification database (Base de Dados de Identificação Civil, BDIC) under the Lei do Registo Eleitoral Oficioso (Law 8/15, as amended). The law mandates intercommunication between the BDCM and the Criminal Records database so that citizens whose political rights are suspended are flagged and separated, and requires the Executive to transmit the resulting citizens' file (Ficheiro Informático dos Cidadãos Maiores) to the National Electoral Commission (CNE) for compiling polling-station maps and electoral rolls. For the 2022 general elections, the CNE operated a dedicated technological platform for registering and identifying candidates, international observers, journalists and electoral police, issuing them dedicated electoral ID cards. Integration remains partial rather than complete: citizens without a Bilhete de Identidade must still register in person, and the African Union Election Observation Mission for the 2022 elections noted continuing data-quality issues, including deceased persons appearing on published voter lists and limited transparency in voter-roll disclosure. A nationwide register update and proof-of-life exercise covering roughly 16.7 million citizens began in June 2026 ahead of the 2027 general elections, continuing to rely on the same civil ID-to-electoral-register data pipeline.
